chapter: Mingus and the call from Hampton
title: Mingus pulls Monk on stage to play with Hampton
summary: At a dance Mingus lifted Monk onto the stage; Hampton gave him a mike; Monk had had his bass less than two years.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: Well, how long after Mingus had been in town did you get the call to go with Hamp?

Well, I got the call after they had gone. Because Wes was working with the band then and...perhaps the following year, I would say, before I heard from them. But what happened that night when they were in town...I'd gone to a dance...then, if you would dance, there'd be like a dance-concert mixed; you'd just sit and listen or you could dance.

And at the end of the night, Hamp was always good at that, if he was in somebody's home town, whoever's home town it is, they'd get a chance to showcase, which is great, you know. That's a real good...that's smart. He was very ring-wise that way. It's whoever, or wherever he's at, that's a town that one of the members...that's his home town, that person stretches out. He's big in that town.

So Wes kind of took over, dominated that night. And really broke it up, because Wes sounded so great with that band. And about the last set, Mingus said...I'm standing watching Mingus all night...he said, 'Come on up here and play some, come on up and play some, I'm tired.' I said, 'Are you kidding?' He said, 'No, I'm not kidding' and he reached down for me, to lift me up on the stage, because it was a kind of a high stage.

And this Mingus come up and play some. He wasn't even asking Hamp could I sit in or anything. They had two bass players so he knew he'd never be missed, he figured. Because they were just playing shouting tunes, they were stretching Wes out anyhow. And I couldn't...I wanted to so badly I couldn't believe it. Really. And he reached down and he helped me up there. I got up the side, and he handed me that bass and I started playing.

The people saw me on stage and they start, like, screaming for me. And Hamp looked over, recognized me being there, he didn't even know I had gotten up and played. And he goes on with it, he's a showman. And he saw, 'Is that what you want? OK, fine.' So he turned me on. He just brought the mike over and let me stretch out too. And there I was, shaking all over, but when I think about that little span of time that I had gotten into playing and here I was at
least on a stage with Lionel Hampton and those guys, the heavies, playing. And that was really a great feeling for me.
Well, actually, how many years elapsed between the time you bought that bass and the time you were standing on that stage?
Yeah. In fact, it was a little under two years because I joined Hamp's band after I had it two and a half years, I was in Hamp's band.
